text:
Boston arrives with its five-game winning streak over after a 3-2 overtime loss at DAL two days ago, though the Bruins have points in six straight and are 4-0-1 in their last five. Nashville comes in rested, four days after a 5-2 win over STL that snapped a three-game winless run (0-1-2). The Predators' last five is 2-1-2.

The model has this nearly even, at 2.93 expected goals for NSH and 2.91 for BOS. Boston has controlled more of the play at five on five, taking 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 45% for Nashville, and its results run ahead of its chances, helped by goaltending. The Bruins also take 4.6 penalties a game, which feeds a Nashville power play averaging 0.62 expected goals a game. Michael DiPietro is the projected Boston starter over Jeremy Swayman, with 1.32 goals saved above expected in two games this season and 0.1 in one game last season. Nashville's goalie isn't confirmed.

For Nashville, Steven Stamkos has a 37% chance to score and Filip Forsberg 36%. Mavrik Bourque could return, cleared from ESPN's injury report. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Adam Edstrom, a third-liner at about 14:45 a night whose shots have been dangerous: 3.0 expected goals in his last eight games, better than 99% of depth forwards. We have him at 19% to score. For Boston, David Pastrnak is 32% to score and 75% to record a point.
